points.titre: The keyboard is now called « De Lëtzebuerger Clavier »
points.texte: That is the name you will see under the icon, in your phone's list of keyboards and on Google Play. Nothing else changes: your words, your cards, your progress and your settings stay as they are.

images.alt: The app's home screen: a blue bar carrying the name « De Lëtzebuerger Clavier », the four tabs Haut, Spiller, Wierderbuch and Mäi Lëtzebuergesch, then the « Configuration rapide » card where step 1, « Activer le clavier » (turn the keyboard on), is ticked and step 2, « Sélectionner le clavier » (pick the keyboard), reads: « Choisissez « De Lëtzebuerger Clavier » dans la liste des claviers qui s'affiche. » (Choose « De Lëtzebuerger Clavier » in the list of keyboards that appears.) A yellow line unrolls under the name in the bar, then a yellow highlighter lights up the same name quoted in step 2: it is the same everywhere.
images.legende: The name in the bar is the one the app asks you to look for on your phone.

images.alt: The phone's « Clavier à l'écran » (on-screen keyboard) settings screen: the Gboard row with its switch off, then the row « 🇱🇺 De Lëtzebuerger Clavier », its red lion icon, switch on in blue.
images.legende: In the phone's list of keyboards, the name shows in full.

points.titre: The translation highlights its word too
points.texte: Under the example sentence, the French word that translates the one on the card or in the dictionary entry now stands out in turn. « ech si vun enger Bei gepickt ginn » and « j'ai été piqué par une abeille » answer each other at a glance. When the translation renders the sentence other than word for word, it stays in plain type rather than point at the wrong word.

images.alt: The entry for the word « Haus » in the app's dictionary: the word in large type, the label « Nom neutre » (neuter noun), the meaning « maison » (house), then the example sentence « mir hunn nach vill Aarbecht ronderëm eist neit Haus » with its translation in grey underneath, « il reste beaucoup de travaux à faire autour de notre maison » (there is still a lot of work to do around our new house), and a second example sentence. A yellow highlighter lights up the word « Haus » in the Luxembourgish sentence first, then the word « maison » in the translation, and both stay lit together.
images.legende: In the dictionary, the translation puts the word it translates in bold.

images.alt: The « Beie » card of the collection, open, bearing the LuxKeyb watermark. Under the drawing of a golden bee in front of the lit façades of a town at nightfall, the plate with the word « Beie », then the text panel: the meaning « abeille » (bee), the example sentence « ech si vun enger Bei gepickt ginn » and its translation « j'ai été piqué par une abeille » (I was stung by a bee). A yellow highlighter lights up the word « Bei » in the sentence first, then the word « abeille » in the translation.
images.legende: On the card too, the Luxembourgish word and the French one answer each other.

points.titre: The word stands out in its example sentence
points.texte: On the collection cards, in the dictionary entry and in the guided tour, the word that the sentence illustrates is now written in bold. You spot it at a glance, even when the sentence uses another form of it, and it is the official dictionary itself that says which word it is: every sentence now has one, including those where nothing pointed to it before.

images.alt: The « Ameis » card of the collection, open, bearing the LuxKeyb watermark. Under the drawing of a golden ant in front of the lit façades of a town at nightfall, the plate with the word « Ameis », then the text panel: the meaning « fourmi » (ant), the example sentence « ënner dem Fënsterbriet haust eng Kolonie Ameisen » with the word « Ameisen » in bold, and its translation « une colonie de fourmis s'est installée sous le rebord de la fenêtre » (a colony of ants has settled under the window ledge).
images.legende: The card's word stands out in its sentence, even in the plural.

points.texte: When you tapped a card in the collection, it stayed hidden behind the dark veil for a moment before turning over. It now turns over almost at once, even on modest phones.
On modest phones, animated cards no longer stutter. The Ferris wheel and the carousel horses of the Schueberfouer turn smoothly again, and swiping from one card to the next happens without a pause.

points.titre: The Mëllerdall as in the photo
points.texte: The Schéissendëmpel card gets back its small moss-covered stone bridge, its three waterfalls dropping from the same pool between two large rocks, and its dark undergrowth where the light passes under the arch.
The pool is a limpid blue, and yellow irises stand with their feet in the water, which you can see through.

images.alt: The landscape of the Mëllerdall card in two views side by side, marked with the LuxKeyb watermark. 1. In the afternoon: in undergrowth of ivy and leaves, the small mossy stone bridge at the back; in front, three waterfalls drop between large green rocks into a turquoise pool where pebbles and a few fish show; in the foreground, yellow irises stand with their feet in the water. 2. The same landscape at night, all in blues, the three waterfalls lit.
images.legende: The Schéissendëmpel in the Mëllerdall, in the afternoon and at night.
